title: Does the shipped application run only under `next dev`, or must it support `next build` / `next start`?
statement: The application shell must declare ONE deployment mode as its supported configuration. Choosing production mode reactivates AST-0010, which was deferred (#137) on the grounds that validating a production build would test an undeclared deployment mode.
notes: ⚠️ This question is a TRIGGER, not only a choice. AST-0010's deferral is conditioned on the deployment mode staying undeclared; declaring `next build` / `next start` is exactly the reopening condition it records, and the validation becomes owed the moment the answer is production. Answering `next dev` only is therefore cheaper AND narrower, and the cost of that narrowness — no evidence that the shipped configuration is the validated one — belongs in the answer rather than being discovered later. ⚠️ PARTIAL RESULT 2026-08-24 — DIRECT RETRIEVAL ONLY, AND THE QUESTION STAYS OPEN. `TAVILY_API_KEY` is not configured, so `research_search` refuses (no-credential, DEC-0006). The credential-free `research_fetch` path does work, so three claims were taken from primary Next.js documentation (v16.3.2, retrieved 2026-08-24) and recorded as assertions with quote-verified evidence: AST-0015 (dev and production are DIFFERENT builds — `.next/dev` versus `.next`), AST-0016 (`next start` is production mode and requires a prior `next build`), and AST-0017 (a self-hosted Node.js deployment supports all Next.js features, with no platform or adapter required). ⚠️ AST-0015 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS FOR THE TRIGGER: because the two builds are genuinely different artifacts, a validation run under `next dev` says nothing about what a production deployment does — which is precisely why #137 could defer AST-0010 while the mode was undeclared, and why declaring production mode makes it owed rather than optional. ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and why the question is not being closed: these three establish the MECHANICS, not the CHOICE. All three sit at rung 2 (`source-supported`) — documentation, not measurement — and the open half is operational rather than documentary: whether a long-lived `next dev` process is sound as the shipped configuration for a local tool, and whether its own file watching interacts badly with the app's chokidar watcher (#73), which bears on REQ-0018 and QST-0021 as much as on this question. Neither is answerable from a documentation page: the first needs discovery across reports the docs do not carry, and the second needs a bounded probe. Closing this now would be deciding a product question from mechanics alone and calling the result researched.
